proposals.spec_text: volatile_write_cache: 'When enabled, flush calls in checkpoint and format paths are conditionally compiled OUT, improving performance...'
proposals.actual: Code compiles flush IN only when the feature is enabled (lib.rs:309-310, checkpoint.rs:102-103) — inverse of spec. AND the feature is non-functional/non-compiling: BlockDeviceClient has no flush() method, and Command::FlushSync / Completion::FlushDone do not exist in the interfaces crate (only the extent-manager mock references them, under the same gate). Enabling --features volatile_write_cache fails to compile in three places across two crates. Cargo.toml + README confirm code INTENT is 'enabled = issue flush'.

options.a_backfill_and_draft: Backfill FR-030 to the real intended semantics (enabled = issue an explicit metadata-device flush after checkpoint/format writes) AND draft the cross-crate compile fix on the branch: add Command::FlushSync + Completion::FlushDone to interfaces/iblock_device.rs, add BlockDeviceClient::flush() (sends FlushSync, awaits FlushDone), and add an actor handler in block-device-spdk-nvme. Flag the actor's NVMe flush opcode for hardware review. Also queue a CI job building with the feature. RECOMMENDED.
options.b_queue_only: Backfill FR-030 semantics but only queue an align-task for the code work (no drafted code this sweep) — safest given it touches the SPDK hardware actor.
options.c_invert_cfg: Treat spec's 'compiled out when enabled' wording as authoritative and invert the #[cfg] gates. WARNING: this makes the DEFAULT build (feature off) call the still-nonexistent flush() -> breaks default build. Not advised.
options.d_defer: Defer; leave the non-functional feature and inverted wording as-is.

proposals.spec_text: FR-016 already documents that iextent_manager.rs:244 and README.md:13 wrongly say 'five minutes' and instructs they be corrected to the true 30-second default.
proposals.actual: Code default is correctly 30s (lib.rs:112); the two doc strings remain stale ('five minutes' / 'default 5 minutes').
proposals.proposed: ALIGN (docs): update iextent_manager.rs:244 and README.md:13 from five-minutes wording to 30 seconds, satisfying FR-016's own remediation clause. Drafted on the feature branch.

proposals.spec_text: capacity_bytes() 'returns the total data device capacity in bytes as configured during format()'.
proposals.actual: Returns buddy total_usable_size (= data_disk_size - data_start_offset). Equals total in separate-device mode; under-reports by the reserved metadata area when metadata_region_size>0 (shared-device mode). lib.rs:710-715.
proposals.proposed: Backfill FR-032 to state it returns the USABLE data capacity (data device size minus any reserved in-device metadata region), matching the implementation and the interfaces-crate wording.

proposals.actual: data_base_lba is stored (lib.rs:98,721) and returned (lib.rs:725) but never applied — this component performs NO data-device I/O; the caller (dispatcher) owns the data path and consumes the offset. metadata_base_lba IS applied.
proposals.proposed: Backfill FR-036 to clarify data_base_lba is a caller-consumed configuration value: the component stores/returns it for the dispatcher to apply to the data path, and performs no internal data-device I/O itself. metadata_base_lba wording unchanged.
